Thanks for taking this. Medicova is evaluating Redwood for inference-on-sensitive-health-data and we need to validate an "EU-only" processing guarantee and the supporting SCCs evidence. Our legal and security teams asked for: 

- A short statement on how you enforce "EU-only" inference (routing, in-region GPUs, and what "in-region" means for backups).
- Whether backups and snapshots are stored outside the EU and the deletion timeline for backups on customer request.
- KMS & key-ownership model: do we control keys (bring-your-own-key) and can you prove key destruction on contract termination?
- Operator access controls / emergency access: logs and attestation we can review.
- Confirmation of Subprocessor list for EU-only workloads and any prior exceptions.

I've attached our SCCs questionnaire (SCCs-Questions-Medicova.pdf) — can you confirm what evidence you can provide and the expected delivery timeframe?

We are trying to finalize an internal decision the week of Nov 27. A short call (30m) this week would help.

Appreciate it,

Subject: Re: EU-only processing / SCCs - technical & evidentiary responses

Simon — following up with the technical breakdown and what we can include in the evidence bundle. I won't repeat everything in the questionnaire, but here's a concise mapping: 

1) EU-only enforcement model
- Routing & locality: for hosted and dedicated we use region tagging at the request ingress layer; for your account we'll pin inference workloads to eu-west-1 / eu-central-1 pools only.  All requests routed to those pools never leave the EU region for compute or KV cache.
- Backups & snapshots: persistent snapshots for dedicated pools are stored in-region by default. We retain a separate cold backup replica that can be geo-restricted; we will provide an attestation listing which storage shards hold your backups.

2) Backups deletion timeline
- Active data deletion (model inputs & ephemeral KV cache): immediate on request; KV namespaces are purged and pointers removed within 24 hours.
- Snapshot/cold backup deletion: scheduled deletion within 30 days of request; we provide a proof-of-deletion artifact (manifest + storage-trim logs) once completed.

3) KMS & key management
- For Private and Dedicated we support BYOK via customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or HSM integration). Keys remain in your control; we do not hold unencrypted copies of customer keys.
- On contract termination, we support either key handover or cryptographic erasure — we provide attestation logs for key destruction.

4) Operator access / emergency processes
- Operator access requires time-limited, audited tickets implemented through our IAM + Privileged Access Workbench. We log all sessions and store session records for 12 months by default; we can increase retention for enterprise customers.
- Evidence bundle will include: operator access runbook excerpt, sample session logs (redacted), and our SOC2 control mappings for access.

5) SCCs & Transfer Impact Assessments (TIA)
- We can provide executed SCCs (standard contractual clauses) as signed PDF and an SCC annex that maps subprocessors and transfer safeguards.
- We maintain a TIA template; where required we can populate it for Medicova with specifics around subprocessors and technical controls (pseudonymization, encryption-in-transit & at-rest).

6) Subprocessors
- We'll provide the current EU subprocessor list and note any non-EU subprocessors that handle control-plane functions (these do not touch content plane for EU-only pinned workloads).

Deliverables & timeline (proposed):
- Day 1: Signed SCCs + subprocessor list (we can provide within 3 business days).
- Day 3-5: Evidence bundle (attestation of backups location, deletion manifest sample, operator access runbook).
- Day 10: TIA draft populated for Medicova review.

I will link the evidence artifacts to a shared folder once available. If you need an on-site or F2F attestation, we can discuss an audit window in the contract.

Best,
